data.ruling: The refutation does not stand. The only failed check is "end-of-life notices". The verifier did not find an end-of-life notice. It failed to reach a PCN (product change notice) URL, which returned HTTP 404, and it marked the check as passing anyway. The Lifecycle check gate reads "any end-of-life notice fails". A listing that could not be read is not an end-of-life notice. Microchip's public PCN listing is readable. The product page links it at https://www.microchip.com/en-us/support/product-change-notification, and that page loads an app backed by a public search API. The re-read found 43 notices matching MCP23017 and none of type "End of Life". None of the 43 titles or document names contains an end-of-life, discontinued, obsolete, last-time-buy or NRND (not recommended for new designs) marking. The notices are manufacturing changes, such as die attach, bond wire and assembly site changes (the latest DSNO-06KMUN607, 2026-08-10), plus data sheet revisions and a 2005 errata. The product page still gives Status "In Production", and Digi-Key gives Active with end_of_life false. The longevity commitment is recorded only (S5 answer, owner 2026-09-25), so its unread policy PDF is not a gate. It was also not among the failed checks. No other check in either verifier's return failed.

- Body {"pageIndex":1,"pageSize":100,"filterText":"MCP23017","filterType":0} (0 = "All"): HTTP 200, totalCount 43, read 2026-09-29T17:33:13Z. A text scan of all 43 records for end-of-life, EOL, discontinu, obsolet, last-time or NRND found 0.

- Control query: filterType 5 with empty filterText gave totalCount 1159 at 17:32:53Z, so the end-of-life filter returns notices.
- The text search matches affected parts. DSNO-06KMUN607 is listed for MCP23017, but its title names no part.
